fatal_errors: The proposed mechanism is fundamentally different from the target: it invokes enhanced interfacial dislocation nucleation, shear-band accumulation, and softening rather than semicoherent-interface blocking, dislocation pileup, possible amorphization, and diffusion/interface-slip-mediated creep resistance.
It substitutes a generic CoCrFeMnNi/refractory-HEA system for the approximately 1 μm Al-Cr-Fe-Ni FCC/BCC multilayers and does not reconstruct the 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm modulation-period comparison.
The baseline is conventional metallic multilayers rather than the coherent M8 and grain-boundary-dominated M32/M80 specimens needed to isolate the anomalous M16 response.
The elevated-temperature range up to 500 °C is unsupported by the target, which establishes only room-temperature nanoindentation behavior.
Neither cited source directly supports progressive interface shear or shear-band formation in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers.
explanation: The response addresses sustained deformation in nanoscale HEA multilayers and proposes a falsifiable in situ experiment, so it has broad problem alignment and some experimental discriminability. However, it misses the central modulation-period/interface-coherency comparison and predicts progressive softening instead of the exceptional creep resistance of the semicoherent 16 nm multilayer. It also omits the stress-exponent signature distinguishing diffusion/interface slip from dislocation creep. E2 concerns deformation in bulk refractory HEAs and supports extensive dislocation nucleation with restricted motion, not multilayer-interface shear; E1 supports nanoindentation as a creep probe and composition-dependent creep resistance but not the proposed mechanism. Thus the central claims are speculative extrapolations rather than an evidence-grounded reconstruction or a well-supported alternative.
